sheet-1-1.description: The western half of Sheet 1 shows the centre of Spotswood along Main Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with Main Street running up the page (north lies to the upper left). It runs from the post office and fire department north of Bridge Street (De Voe Avenue) south past the cemetery to South Street, where the street continues on the right half of the same sheet. At Bridge Street, Vliet Lane (Vliet Avenue) leaves Main Street westward, and below it New Brunswick Road branches off to the southwest, crossing the Pennsylvania Railroad (Amboy Division) and meeting Adirondack Avenue and Madison Avenue at the lower left corner, where a row of narrow lots is laid out. Along Main Street stand dwellings, stores, two hotels, a garage, the post office and fire department (Fire Dept.), the Spotswood Public Library, the Episcopal church (Episc'l Church, with a 40 ft spire) and Episcopal chapel beside the cemetery, a cement block works, the West End Hotel and a sanitarium with a 5000 gallon water tank. The Spotswood Public School lies west of Main Street, and a synagogue and a cork factory stand on New Brunswick Road. Manalapan Brook winds through the open land east of Main Street, with the De Voe Snuff Company buildings beside the heavy dividing line, and Cedar Brook runs south past Main Street. The sheet also carries the Sanborn title cartouche, a legend (key), a compass rose and a small location map of New Jersey; the legend and location map are cut out of the mask.
notes: Bridge (De Voe Av.) is today's De Voe Avenue; Vliet Lane (Vliet Av.) is today's Vliet Street.
New Brunswick Road is today's Snowhill Street; Main Street south of the New Brunswick Road fork is today's Manalapan Road.
Cross-references to Sheet 2 at the top of Main Street and to the right half of Sheet 1 at South Street.

Main Street / Vliet Street / De Voe Avenue is drawn as two offset junctions (Vliet Lane and Bridge do not meet Main at one point); the modern junction was left out of the control (see the sheet note).

Map, 100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 Main Street (Bridge St to South St) with New Brunswick Rd (Snowhill Street), Adirondack and Madison Avs; part 2 Main Street (Manalapan Road) south of South St with John St and Grand Av, drawn at about 10 degrees different rotation. Title cartouche, key and location map cut out of the masks. Main / Vliet / De Voe junction excluded on part 1: drawn as two offset junctions; with it LOO 6.4 m, without 4.8 m (hand-picks at the drawn centres made it worse, 14.9 m).

sheet-1-2.description: The eastern half of Sheet 1 continues Main Street south of South Street, drawn as a separate strip beside the town centre and at a slightly different rotation. Main Street runs up the page from Grand Avenue at the bottom to South Street at the top, with John Street leaving it eastward. West of Main Street run the Pennsylvania Railroad (Amboy Division) and Cedar Brook, with the Spotswood Grain Co. elevator (capacity 10,000 bushels, built 1923) beside the tracks. The frontages are lined with dwellings, small outbuildings and a few stores; the Methodist Church stands on the east side of Main Street just south of South Street. A small brook crosses the lower right corner near Grand Avenue, and the east edge is marked as having no exposures. The strip is divided from the left half of the sheet by a heavy line; the sheet's title cartouche sits above it and is cut out of the mask.
notes: Main Street here is today's Manalapan Road.
Grand Av. is not in the modern street data used for control; only South Street and John Street junctions were used.

Map, 100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 Main Street (Bridge St to South St) with New Brunswick Rd (Snowhill Street), Adirondack and Madison Avs; part 2 Main Street (Manalapan Road) south of South St with John St and Grand Av, drawn at about 10 degrees different rotation. Title cartouche, key and location map cut out of the masks. Main / Vliet / De Voe junction excluded on part 1: drawn as two offset junctions; with it LOO 6.4 m, without 4.8 m (hand-picks at the drawn centres made it worse, 14.9 m).

sheet-2-1.description: The right part of Sheet 2 shows Main Street north of the town centre, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street running up the page. Summer Hill Road leaves Main Street to the northwest about halfway up the part, crossing toward the Pennsylvania Railroad (Amboy Division), which runs along the left edge of the part. The frontages are thinly built with dwellings, barns and sheds on deep lots; the 1st Reformed Church (with a 38 ft spire) and a cemetery stand east of Main Street near the bottom. A small brook crosses the part from the lower left to the right edge, and the east edge is marked as having no exposures. Cross-references at the bottom lead to Sheet 1 and at the top to the left part of this sheet, which continues Main Street further north. The part is divided from the insets and the left strip by a heavy diagonal line.
notes: Summer Hill Rd. is today's Summerhill Road.

Map, 100 ft. Four parts: 1 Main Street at Summer Hill Rd (right); 2 inset Bloomfield Mills Co. licorice works, 1 1/4 miles north of Spotswood; 3 inset De Voe Snuff Co. on Bridge St and Manalapan Brook; 4 Main Street further north with the P.R.R., no cross streets (left strip). Only part 1 configured.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: The Bloomfield Mills Co., manufacturers of licorice, on South River, located 1 1/4 miles north of Spotswood (no street drawn; outside the reference box; needs site identification and parcel or building corners).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: De Voe Snuff Co. on Bridge Street and Manalapan Brook (Tail Race, pond) (one street only (Bridge Street, now De Voe Avenue), no junction; needs step 6b: carried points from sheet-1-1 (storage building, bridge) or parcel corners).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Main Street north of Summer Hill Road with the P.R.R. (Amboy Division), house numbers 438 to 534 (no street junction (Main Street only); needs step 6b: carried points from sheet-2-1 or parcel corners along Main Street).
